newsitem.title: USA: Latin debt prices rally after U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Latin debt prices rally after U.S. jobs data.

text.p: Emerging market debts shook off days of lethargy to rally strongly on the back of U.S. Treasuries fueled by friendly U.S. jobs data, traders said.

The U.S. Labor Department reported that 250,000 new non-farm jobs were created in August and the unemployment rate fell to seven-year low at 5.1 percent. The evidence the U.S. economy is going strong without overheating spurred advances in both the U.S. bond and the U.S. stock markets.
"Emerging market paper has outperformed Treasuries," said a European bank trader, who noted fresh buying from funds.
Argentina led among Latin Bradies to spring higher, followed by equally hearty demand for Brazil and Venezuela papers, Brady traders said.
Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR rose 1-/18 to 79-7/8, while Brazilian Cs BR8D14=RR gained 1-1/4 to 65-3/8.
Mexican and Ecuadorean paper belatedly caught up with the other Latin Bradies, traders said.
Ecuador paper had a shaky start. News the head of the central bank, Augusto de la Torre, tendered his resignation caused some confusion. The resignation was refused by the government.

Analysts described the resignation as a formality, as de la Torre is a hold-over from former President Sixto Duran Ballen's administration. President Abdala Bucaram, upon taking office on August 10, asked de la Torre to remain in the post.
But a senior government source told Reuters the resignation was made because of differing viewpoints. De la Torre will meet President Bucaram on Monday.
Mexico's fast recovery in the second quarter may be setting some investors up for disappointment as expectations ran ahead of the reality, one analyst said.
"The consumption in durable goods is still weak and the jobs growth remains at the low-end of the labor market," said Omar Borla, Latin America economist at Robert Flemings Inc.
Some investors have used the uprising of the guerrillas in the southern states as opportunities to lighten up their positions, he added.
